title.fallback: A Cure for the Common Death

summary.fallback: Doctor Edrin Vale claims he is close to a cheaper cure for zombification. Bring him the first ingredients for his restorative.

intro.fallback: You're the one they told me about, yes? Good. Come closer. I need someone with a strong stomach and a flexible definition of medicine.

offer.fallback: Physician, natural philosopher, and increasingly unwilling customer of clerics. Zombification should not require a golden apple and a small miracle every time.
You think you can cure it another way?
I think dead flesh is not dead so much as badly instructed. Give it the correct instructions and it may remember what shape it used to be.
Rotten flesh for comparison, honey to slow decay, and redstone to keep the reaction awake. Nothing dangerous. If it explodes, it will be a very small explosion.

return.fallback: Excellent. The tissue is reacting already. Do not be alarmed by the twitching. Twitching is considerably closer to life than not twitching.

return_steps.fallback: Only locally. A hand remembering that it once belonged to an arm is not the same thing as a resurrection.
That distinction does not comfort me.
Comfort has delayed more discoveries than ignorance ever did.

reward.fallback: You supplied the first proper trial. Take this, and come back when I have something alive enough to disappoint me.

done.fallback: The first batch is stable. Stable is a generous word, but it is the word I am using.
